market_holds: Spot $48.12 at 18:10 UTC on 2026-11-09 (sealed baseline). It is up 74% over 20 sessions and 15% over 5, and up about 79% from the $26.81 close on 2026-10-13, the eve of the settlement. It is still about 31% below the ~$70 level before the 2026-09-30 '327 PH-ILD ruling (Yahoo daily bars). The headline quarter is already public: preliminary Q3 YUTREPIA net sales were $222.7m, +31% QoQ, and cash was $396.1m (8-K, 2026-10-14). The settlement is also public: $175m due within 30 business days, $145.4m in Jan and Apr 2027, $60.3m paid to third parties in October. The PH-ILD label is to be removed, and Liquidia has stopped promoting and selling YUTREPIA for PH-ILD. On 2026-11-04 the stock rose 12.3% (42.20 to 47.38) when United Therapeutics reported Q3 before the open and said existing YUTREPIA PH-ILD patients are not required to switch and that it expects only moderate switching. Options: straddle to 11-13 at 11.8%, event-implied move 6.8% (the ATM spread is 78% of mid, so this is indicative only), 25-delta skew +15.6 vol points, so downside protection is being paid for. The usual move is a median 3.5%, but the last two prints moved +25.6% and -10.5%. Consensus is thin and stale: on Nasdaq, Q3 EPS is $0.77 from 2 estimates with no revisions in 4 weeks; Q4 is $0.11 with a range of -0.47 to +0.70; FY2027 is $2.13 with a range of 0.95 to 4.00. Short interest was 17.3m shares (~19% of the ~88.9m shares outstanding) at the 2026-10-15 settlement date, up from 12.6m on 09-30; the 10-31 figure is not yet published. The line the stock trades on: the post-settlement PAH-only demand trajectory (October patient starts, PH-ILD retention, the Q4 and 2027 run-rate) and the cash path through the settlement payments, not the already-known Q3 sales.
view: This print is the first time management quantifies life after the settlement. The Q3 revenue and cash numbers are pre-announced and priced. GAAP EPS will very likely carry a settlement charge and screen as a large 'miss' against a stale $0.77, which informed holders will look through. What decides the reaction by 13:00 ET is the call: October/November new patient starts, how much of the patient base is PH-ILD and whether it stays on therapy, and whatever Q4/2027 framing management gives. The evidence points both ways. Against: (1) new prescriptions were roughly equal between PAH and PH-ILD as of the 2026-03-05 call, so cutting PH-ILD promotion and sales roughly halves the new-start engine; (2) United Therapeutics reported record referrals in October (>1,000 for a single UT product), with an inflection from mid-September, which suggests YUTREPIA's share of new starts fell in Q4; (3) the stock has already recovered ~79% off the low, with the largest leg of the last week coming on UTHR's 'no forced switching' comment, so a good deal of reassurance is already in the price; (4) skew shows downside being paid for. For: (1) about 19% of shares outstanding were short as of mid-October and many of those shorts were added at the lows, so a reassuring PAH growth message or stable Q4 could squeeze hard (May's print moved +25.6%); (2) the existing PH-ILD base looks retained per UTHR, so near-term revenue may hold up better than the 2027 consensus low end of $0.95 implies; (3) cash plus ~$90m+/quarter of operating profit covers the payments with no financing, which management has already said. I cannot show which way management's October numbers will land against what the price holds. The market has already reacted twice to the main facts (the settlement +27%, the UTHR call +12%), so I lean very slightly to a give-back after the run-up, but not enough to recommend.

recommendation.reason: The decisive information is management's post-settlement demand data (October starts, PH-ILD retention, Q4/2027 framing), and no public trace of it exists before the call. The market has already repriced the two public facts that bear on it: the settlement terms, and UTHR's statement that existing PH-ILD patients need not switch. A heavy short base (~19% of shares outstanding) and a ~79% run-off-the-lows pull in opposite directions, so I cannot reach 65% on direction.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Management saying total patients on therapy and Q4 net sales are still growing QoQ, with PH-ILD patients retained, would push me toward up (squeeze risk). Disclosing that PH-ILD was well over half of patients, or that October new starts fell sharply, would push me toward down.

self_critique: The strongest case for up: ~19% of shares were short in mid-October, and coverage is thin and anchored on stale numbers. If management shows Q4 net sales still rising on PAH and a retained PH-ILD base, plus a clean cash bridge, shorts covering into a 13:00 exit could produce a double-digit gain like May's +25.6%. The strongest case for a sharper down: October new starts probably fell hard, since the ruling caused two weeks of prescriber uncertainty and promotion then ceased, and the stock has rallied ~79% on reassurance that came from UTHR rather than from Liquidia's own data. Neither side can be shown from public data before the call, so p_up stays near 50.
approach_notes: P4 (prove 'priced') helped: tying the 11-04 +12% to UTHR's switching comment showed that reassurance was already priced. P3's 'stakeholder calls' route (UTHR's call) was the only fresh data source. The decisive information sits inside the call itself, so the loop ended quickly at no recommendation, as P8 allows.
